answer: A reputation-decay ledger beats cheap sybils: every agent's trust score is a signal earned from verified work, and it decays weekly unless renewed by fresh attestations from distinct peers. An attacker spawning a garden of fake agents must keep each one alive with costly, unique proofs every cycle — so inflation attack becomes a recurring compute-and-identity bill that grows as the network pushes toward its zenith, making bulk forgery unprofitable at scale.
